extracted.intended_audience: parents, youth ministry leaders, and readers concerned about children’s media exposure (audience of CPYU)
extracted.subtask_description: A short opinion/blog guidance on how to judge advertising and media that involve young children, with emphasis on protecting children, cultural impact, and parental equipping in discernment. Uses the Balenciaga campaign as a current-events exemplar.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sexualized depiction of children
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything related to child pornography or trafficking is wrong; the Balenciaga ads featured very young children posing with Teddy Bear handbags in BDSM gear (leather straps and metal spikes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post emphasizes that sexualized imagery involving toddlers is inappropriate and alarming; such content has prompted strong backlash and legal/ethical concerns. Use this as a firm boundary: do not create, approve, or publish imagery that sexualizes children or references sexual practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that ads transmit a worldview
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads do sell product. But what they sell more than anything else is a worldview . . . a way of looking at, interpreting, and living life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing advertising, consider not only commercial effectiveness but also the underlying values and messages being normalized. Ask how imagery and themes shape cultural attitudes, especially about vulnerable populations like children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility and ensure accountability in production decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone involved in the ad campaign is pointing fingers of blame at others for the fact that the ad was created and released; the fact that it was created and released is a clear indicator that we've lost our bearings on what is and isn't appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should have clear internal safeguards and decision‑making processes to prevent inappropriate content from being approved. Evaluate the chain of approval, creative oversight, and who signs off on potentially sensitive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate corrective action for offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to the backlash, Balenciaga has pulled the ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offensive or harmful content is released, prompt removal and acknowledgement are necessary first steps. Use corrective actions as part of damage control and as an indicator of taking responsibility, but also review how the error occurred to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controversies as teachable examples to equip children
rubrics_metrics.description: The Balenciaga campaign might serve today as 'Exhibit A' for the need to [teach discernment]; parents need to be equipping our kids with skills in biblical discernment that will serve them both now and for the rest of their lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage real-world incidents to prompt conversations with children about media, values, and boundaries. Provide practical resources and training (for example the cited book and podcast) so children can critically interpret cultural messages and resist harmful normalization.
